title: The Cooling Curve
primary_metric: watts of heat dissipated per dollar of fin manufacturing cost

options.A: Spec the Pyramid Array — pyramidal fins machined into every cold plate in the deployment
options.B: Spec the Cone Standoffs — conical standoff fins machined into every cold plate in the deployment

_ext: keys below are pipeline extensions, additive to SPEC §4

deliverables.text: A volume-per-fin table: volume of material in one Pyramid Array fin (pyramid) and one Cone Standoff fin (cone), from the Appendix B dimensions.
A surface-area-per-fin table: total exposed surface area of one Pyramid Array fin and one Cone Standoff fin, from the Appendix B dimensions, as the basis for each design's heat-dissipation rate.
A manufacturing-cost-per-fin table: convert each fin's D1 volume into a material cost, add the mold-amortization cost from Appendix C, for a fully-loaded cost per fin per design.

A watts-per-dollar comparison table: D2 surface area x Appendix A dissipation rate, divided by D3 cost per fin, scaled to the Appendix E deployment fin count, cross-checked against the Appendix D benchmark.
A recommendation stating which fin geometry the site should tool up for, defended against the deployment's mold-order deadline in Appendix E.

appendices.title: ASHRAE TC9.9 Thermal Guidelines: Heat Dissipation and Surface Area
Fin Geometry Spec Sheet: Pyramid vs. Cone

balance.argument_a: The Pyramid Array's four flat faces expose strictly more surface area than a cone sharing the same base footprint and height, and Appendix A ties heat dissipation directly to exposed surface area — so per fin, the pyramid moves more heat. If the deployment's thermal margin is tight, more watts dissipated per fin (even at a higher per-fin cost) can win on watts-per-dollar once the mold cost is amortized across the tens of thousands of fins this deployment needs — mold cost is a one-time cost, but every fin's extra surface area pays back on every one of the deployment's cooling cycles.
balance.argument_b: The Cone Standoffs use a shape-of-revolution mold — cheaper and faster to tool than a four-face pyramid mold — and that cost difference is paid on every single fin cast from it, not once. At data-center volumes, a modest per-fin cost gap compounds across tens of thousands of fins into a real budget swing, and if the cone's smaller surface-area deficit turns out to cost the deployment less heat dissipation than its mold-cost savings are worth, the cheaper-to-tool geometry wins on the metric that actually matters: watts per dollar, not watts alone.
balance.margin_basis: Compare each design's watts-per-dollar figure (D4: [D2 surface area x Appendix A dissipation rate] / D3 cost per fin) once Appendix A's dissipation rate, Appendix B's dimensions, and Appendix C's material/mold costs are sourced or stated as Modeling Assumptions by case-research.
